{"body":"# Telling the truth on screen at the counter

## In plain words

An integration that overstates its own state is worse than one that reports a
gap, because the gap is then discovered by a patient at a counter rather than by
the person who could have fixed it.

Most of what follows was a defect before it was a rule.

## Before you start

- The six screens, from [the screen contract](m1-screen-contract.md), because
  several of these rules are about where a message lands.

## What happens

**An error must land on the screen the person is looking at.** A multi step
journey that writes a failure into a step the view has scrolled past shows the
desk nothing at all. Resolve the target to the active step rather than to a
fixed position on the page.

**Accepted is not done.** Anything asynchronous has at least five outcomes and
they must not look alike: sent, accepted and waiting, answered, refused before
it ever waited, and no answer inside the window. A refusal shown as a completion
is the worst of the five.

**A silence is not a failure.** Where no timeout is published, say that nothing
arrived in the window you chose, rather than saying it failed.

**Show the masked number the code went to.** A person with two handsets needs to
know which one to pick up.

**A resend button has two jobs either side of one boundary.** While the
transaction still has attempts left, reuse it, because starting a new one throws
away a live transaction. Once it is locked, only a fresh transaction recovers
and retrying cannot. Show a visible wait, because the fastest route to a locked
transaction is somebody pressing resend four times.

**Name the field, not the person.** When an encrypted value is refused, the
cause is usually the encryption, the headers or the clock. Telling a patient
their number is wrong is usually a lie.

Some of this is interface mechanics rather than ABDM, and it still costs real
failures. Off screen is not hidden: a translated step track leaves every step in
the tab order, so the first keypress walks into fields nobody can see, and
inactive steps need marking inert. State from one patient must not survive into
the next, and the field that leaks is always the one the desk typed rather than
the one the profile filled, because every other field is overwritten on the way
in.

## How you know it worked

Trigger a refusal on the last step of a long journey. The message appears on the
step in view, and the desk can read it without scrolling.

Trigger a synchronous refusal on an asynchronous call. The screen says refused,
not waiting, and not done.

Complete a journey for one patient and start another. No field carries a value
from the first, including the fields the desk typed by hand.

## When it goes wrong

- A green state is showing for a refusal. The success and failure paths are
  sharing a function that closes the waiter. Fix it in the shared function, not
  at each call site.
- A one time password transaction locks repeatedly. Resend is starting a new
  transaction while the old one still had attempts left.
- A patient is told their Aadhaar number is wrong when the clock or the
  certificate is at fault. Name the field that was refused and say what else
  can cause it.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.m1-honest-screen-states","milestone":"M1","summary":"A screen must not say verified, linked or complete when it means accepted, and an error must land where the person is actually looking.","title":"Telling the truth on screen at the counter","type":"concept"}

{"body":"# Present the filled form for confirmation rather than saving it unseen

## In plain words

The point of reading an ABHA profile is that the receptionist stops typing. The
temptation that follows is to stop showing the form at all: the data is
authoritative, so save it and move on.

Do not. The profile is what ABDM holds, which is not the same as what the
clinician needs to see. Names may be transliterated into a script the desk does
not use. An address may be years old. A mobile number on a shared handset may
belong to a relative. None of that makes the profile wrong, and all of it
matters at a counter.

## Before you start

- A form that opens filled, from
  [the counter journey order](m1-counter-journey-order.md).
- [The screen contract](m1-screen-contract.md), whose last screen is this one.

## What happens

The confirmation screen collects corrections only. It asks for nothing the
profile already carries, because everything it carries is already on the
screen.

It is the one screen never skipped. Every other screen in the journey exists to
reach this one with more fields filled.

Show which fields came from the profile, so a correction is a deliberate act
rather than a guess. A receptionist who cannot tell a prefilled value from a
typed one will either trust all of it or retype all of it, and both defeat the
purpose.

A correction changes the facility's record. It does not change what ABDM holds:
the profile is the patient's, updated through their own application or through
the profile update calls, not by a desk editing a form. If the desk's copy and
ABDM's copy need to agree, that is a separate update call and a separate
decision.

## How you know it worked

Register a patient whose profile carries a transliterated name. The
confirmation screen shows the profile's value, the receptionist corrects it,
and the facility record carries the correction.

Read what ABDM holds for that patient afterwards. It is unchanged, because a
correction to the form is not an update to the profile.

## When it goes wrong

- **The record is saved without anybody seeing it.** The form was skipped
  because the data was authoritative. Authoritative is not the same as
  appropriate for this counter.
- **A correction silently changed the ABHA profile.** The form was wired to the
  profile update call. Those are different decisions and usually different
  permissions.
- **The receptionist retypes every field.** Nothing distinguished a prefilled
  value from an empty one, so none of them were trusted.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.m1-confirm-the-filled-form","milestone":"M1","summary":"The profile is what ABDM holds, which is not always what the clinician needs to see, so the filled form is confirmed by a person before it becomes the facility's record.","title":"Present the filled form for confirmation rather than saving it unseen","type":"concept"}

{"body":"# A journey has to complete without an ABHA

## In plain words

An ABHA is voluntary. A person can be treated, registered and billed without
one, and a facility's own patient number is what its record is keyed by.

So a registration journey that cannot finish until an ABHA exists has quietly
decided that people without one are not registered. Nobody chose that. It fell
out of putting the ABHA step first and making the form wait for it. The step
comes first so the form opens filled; it does not come first so the form can be
refused.

## Before you start

- The journey order, from
  [the ABHA step before the form](m1-counter-journey-order.md), because this
  rule is the other half of it.
- The screens, from [the screen contract](m1-screen-contract.md), because the
  exit from the ABHA step has to lead somewhere.

## What happens

Decide it deliberately, and write the decision down where the journey is
designed. The question is not whether to offer an ABHA, which every deployment
does. It is what the desk does when the person has none and cannot or will not
create one now.

The answer for a facility record is that the form still completes. The patient
number is the facility's own. The ABHA fields on that record stay empty, and
[the surface](m1-counter-journey-order.md) offers creation again on the next
visit rather than blocking this one.

The ABHA step therefore needs an exit that is neither success nor failure: not
now. It returns whatever facts it collected to the fact store, and the form
opens with those filled and the rest blank, exactly as it would after a
successful step with fewer fields.

Where a deployment does require an ABHA, a government scheme that pays only
against one for instance, that is a rule of the deployment, and it belongs in
[the deployment interview](m1-deployment-interview.md) as a question with a
yes, not in the screen order as an accident.

## How you know it worked

Walk a patient through the journey and decline the ABHA step at every point it
is offered. The registration completes, the record exists under the facility's
number, and its ABHA fields are empty.

Open the design and find the sentence that says what happens without an ABHA.
It exists, and it was written on purpose.

## When it goes wrong

- **The form will not submit with the ABHA fields empty.** A validation rule
  made the fields required. They are not, unless the deployment interview said
  so.
- **The ABHA step has only two exits.** Success and failure, and a person with
  no ABHA is routed to failure. Add the third exit, not now, and route it to
  the form.
- **The decision was never made.** Nobody can say what the journey does for a
  person without an ABHA. That is this rule failing, whatever the screens do.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.m1-journey-completes-without-abha","milestone":"M1","summary":"An ABHA is voluntary, so a registration that cannot finish without one refuses care to the people who do not have one, and the decision has to be made on purpose rather than fall out of the screen order.","title":"A journey has to complete without an ABHA","type":"concept"}

From the coordinator, a small contract clarification; no reply needed.

- **ABHA address input.** For `identifier_type: "abha_address"`, the user may type the address with or without the suffix, for example `john.doe` or `john.doe@sbx`.
  - The backend appends `@{cm_id}` when there is no `@`.
  - In the UI, show the suffix as an input adornment or hint taken from `config.abha_address_suffix`, rather than requiring it.
  - Do not reject input that already has `@sbx`.
- **Unknown address.** An address that doesn't exist comes back as 404 `abha_not_found`, the same as the other identifiers. Handle it on the shared "not found" screen.
  - For an ABHA address, the most likely cause is a typo. Offer "check the address" (edit) first, and creation as a secondary action.
- **Status.** The backend is still building. I'll message you as soon as it's serving on :9100 with any contract deviations.

{"body":"# What an ABHA address is allowed to be

## In plain words

ABHA Addresses must comply with defined validation standards.

**Permitted Characters**

- Alphabetic characters (A-Z)
- Numeric characters (0-9)
- Dot (.)

**Validation Rules**

- Cannot begin with a numeric character.
- Cannot begin or end with a dot (.).
- Must conform to ABDM validation requirements at the time of creation.
- Mobile numbers cannot be used directly as ABHA Addresses.

Organizations should rely on ABDM validation services to verify address eligibility.

Every ABHA number is issued a default address built from its 14 digits. A person cannot create that address themselves, and can create a readable one beside it. Offer addresses built from the person's name rather than an empty field.

## Before you start

Know whether the address is being created against an ABHA number or against a mobile number with a self declared profile. See [P1 Registration and login](/docs/hiecm/v3/milestones/p1).

## What happens

Validate the rules above in your own form before you submit, so a refused address becomes an inline message. Offer the suggestions the service returns from `/abha/api/v3/enrollment/enrol/suggestion` during M1 enrolment. Send the chosen address without the `@` suffix where the call asks for it.

## How you know it worked

The address is created and the person can sign in with it. Before that, your form refuses an address that begins with a digit, begins or ends with a dot, or is a mobile number.

## When it goes wrong

content.text:
From the coordinator: a contract revision that **simplifies** your Aadhaar handling. Design doc §7 step 5 is updated.

1. **Aadhaar always enrols.** When the user picks **Aadhaar** as the identifier, always use the enrolment endpoints, never `otp/request` with `identifier_type=aadhaar`.
   - Show the consent checkbox, then `POST abdm/abha/create/otp {aadhaar, consent}`.
   - The OTP step asks for the OTP plus "Mobile number for ABHA communication".
   - Then `POST abdm/abha/create/verify {transaction_id, otp, mobile}`.
   - ABDM returns the **existing** ABHA when one exists, with `is_new: false`. That gives one OTP for both outcomes; the old route risked asking for two.
2. **Existing ABHA.** On `is_new: false`, show "An ABHA already exists for this Aadhaar". Go to the result screen (profile card, then the placement's primary action) and skip the mobile-verify and address steps.
   - Exception: still show the address step if `abha_address_required` is true.
   - `mobile_verification_required` will be false for existing accounts.
3. **New ABHA.** On `is_new: true`, continue the create steps as designed: optional mobile verify, then address.
4. **Not found.** "Create ABHA with Aadhaar", offered after `abha_not_found` from other identifiers, goes **straight to `create/otp`**. There is no lookup first. Reuse the Aadhaar and consent if they were already entered.
5. **Unchanged.** Linking still uses `POST patient/{id}/abha/link/ {transaction_id}` with that create transaction, and `existing_patient` is still in the `create/verify` response.

No reply is needed.

content.text:
From the coordinator: **REVERT my previous "Aadhaar always enrols" revision. The original design stands.** Sorry for the churn. Design doc §7 step 5 is restored and annotated.

**Why.** The catalogue atom `hiecm.concept.m1-avoiding-duplicate-abha` says it explicitly:
- "Every identifier starts on the login path, Aadhaar included. Wiring Aadhaar straight to enrolment ... sends everybody who already holds an ABHA to make a second one."
- "Run a login for an identifier nobody holds. You receive 404 with ABDM-1114, **no one time password is sent**, and only then does the journey offer creation."

So looking up first costs exactly **one OTP** in both outcomes. My two-OTP worry was wrong.

**The flow, as originally designed:**
1. User picks Aadhaar. Show the consent text and checkbox, then call `POST abdm/abha/otp/request {identifier_type:"aadhaar", value, consent}`.
   - **Found:** an OTP is sent. Go to the OTP step and call `otp/verify` as normal.
   - **404 `abha_not_found`:** no OTP was sent. Show "No ABHA found for this Aadhaar. Create one?" On confirm, call `POST abdm/abha/create/otp {aadhaar, consent}`, reusing the Aadhaar and consent already given; never ask twice. Then the OTP step with OTP + "Mobile number for ABHA communication", then `create/verify`.
2. `abha_not_found` from other identifiers: "Create ABHA" asks only for Aadhaar plus consent, then **still looks it up first** with `otp/request identifier_type=aadhaar`. Create only on a second `abha_not_found`.

**Keep from my previous message:**
- Handle `is_new:false` from `create/verify` gracefully, as a rare safety net: show "An ABHA already exists for this Aadhaar" and go to the result. Skip mobile verify, and skip the address step unless `abha_address_required`.
- The ABHA address input and suffix guidance still stands.

No reply needed.

## 6. REST API contract (backend implements; frontend consumes)

All endpoints are under `/api/v1/` and use CARE JWT auth unless marked otherwise.

### 6.1 Error shape

All errors use CARE's existing envelope, so `handleHttpError` keeps working:

```json
{"errors": [{"type": "abha_not_found", "msg": "No ABHA was found for this identifier.", "abdm_code": "ABDM-1114", "loc": ["value"], "retry_after_seconds": null}]}
```

| HTTP | `type` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `validation_error` | Our input validation failed (pydantic; `loc` set). |
| 400 | `abdm_validation_error` | ABDM refused a field. `loc` holds our field name; `msg` is ABDM's message, worded so it never blames the patient. |
| 400 | `invalid_otp` / `otp_expired` | |
| 400 | `transaction_expired` / `invalid_state` | Wrong step for this transaction, or the transaction expired. |
| 400 | `consent_required` | Aadhaar was sent without `consent.agreed=true` and the current version. |
| 400 | `abha_linked_to_other_patient` | Include `patient: {id, name, can_view}`. |
| 400 | `patient_already_linked` | The patient is already linked to a **different** ABHA. |
| 400 | `creation_method_not_allowed` | Anything other than Aadhaar was used to create. |
| 404 | `abha_not_found` | **Only** for `ABDM-1114`. |
| 404 | `transaction_not_found` | |
| 429 | `resend_too_soon` | Includes `retry_after_seconds`. |
| 429 | `resend_limit_reached` | |
| 502 | `abdm_unavailable` | Network error, timeout, or ABDM 5xx. |
| 502 | `abdm_error` | Unclassified ABDM refusal; `abdm_code` and `msg` pass through. |
| 502 | `abdm_session_expired` | The X-token expired. The frontend restarts verification. |
| 503 | `abdm_disabled` | |

Never return HTTP 401 or 403 for an ABDM-side auth failure. The frontend treats 401 as "CARE session expired".

```ts
  district_name: string | null; district_code: string | null;
  kyc_verified: boolean;
  status: string | null;               // "ACTIVE" etc.
  photo: string | null;                // base64 JPEG; returned live, NEVER stored
};
type AbhaAccount = {                  // account chooser row (verify may return several)
  abha_number: string | null; abha_address: string | null; name: string;
  gender: string | null; kyc_verified: boolean | null; status: string | null; photo: string | null;
};
type OtpSent = {
  transaction_id: string;              // our opaque uuid
  message: string;                     // ABDM's message, safe to show
  masked_mobile: string | null;        // e.g. "******1234", parsed from the message
  otp_system: "aadhaar" | "abdm";
  resend: { available_in_seconds: number; remaining: number }; // 60 and 2 after the first send
};
type ExistingPatient = { id: string; name: string; can_view: boolean } | null;
type Verified = {
  transaction_id: string;
  status: "verified" | "select_account";
  accounts: AbhaAccount[];             // filled when status = "select_account"
  profile: AbhaProfile | null;         // filled when status = "verified"
  existing_patient: ExistingPatient;   // a CARE patient already linked to this ABHA
};
```

### 6.3 Endpoints

**Configuration**

- `GET /api/v1/abdm/config/`
  - Returns `{enabled, cm_id, abha_address_suffix, consent:{code, version, text}, otp:{length:6, resend_wait_seconds:60, max_resends:2}}`.
  - `consent.text` is the exact ABDM consent text from §8. The backend owns it.

**Identify (login, verify)**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/request/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{identifier_type:"mobile"|"aadhaar"|"abha_number"|"abha_address", value, otp_system?:"aadhaar"|"abdm", consent?:{agreed:true, version:"1.4"}, facility?:uuid}`.
  - `otp_system` is required for `abha_number` and `abha_address`. For the other identifiers it is implied: `aadhaar` → `aadhaar`, `mobile` → `abdm`.
  - `consent` is **required** when `identifier_type="aadhaar"`. The Aadhaar consent is shown before any Aadhaar leaves the browser, and an `AbhaConsent` row is recorded with purpose `aadhaar_verification`.
  - Values: Aadhaar is 12 digits (Verhoeff check). Mobile is 10 digits starting 6–9. The ABHA number is 14 digits, with or without hyphens. The ABHA address may omit the `@sbx` suffix; the backend appends `@{cm_id}`.
  - Returns 404 `abha_not_found` when ABDM answers `ABDM-1114`. In that case no OTP was sent, and the frontend offers creation.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/resend/`
  - Body: `{transaction_id}`. Works for any OTP step: login, find, create, create-mobile and update-mobile.
  - Returns `OtpSent`, or 429.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/verify/` → `Verified`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`. For login and find flows.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/select-account/` → `Verified` (status `verified`)
  - Body: `{transaction_id, abha_number}`.

**Find**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/find/`
  - Body: `{mobile}`.
  - Returns `{transaction_id, accounts:[{index, abha_number (masked), name (masked), gender, kyc_verified, auth_methods:["AADHAAR_OTP","MOBILE_OTP",...]}]}`.
  - Returns 404 `abha_not_found` when ABDM finds none.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/find/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, index, otp_system:"aadhaar"|"abdm"}`.
  - Then call `otp/verify`.

**Create (Aadhaar only)**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{aadhaar, consent:{agreed:true, version:"1.4"}, facility?}`.
  - Records `AbhaConsent` with purpose `abha_creation`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/verify/`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp, mobile}`.
  - Returns `{transaction_id, is_new, profile: AbhaProfile, mobile_verification_required: boolean, abha_address_required: boolean, existing_patient}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/verify/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address-suggestions/?transaction_id=`
  - Returns `{suggestions: string[]}`, without the suffix.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, abha_address}`, without the suffix.

**Verified-session operations** (any flow that reached `enrolled` or `verified`)

- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/?transaction_id=` → `{profile}` (refetched live)
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/card/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
  - `data` is base64 of the official ABHA card. For the address path, this is the PHR card.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/qr/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/verify/` → `{profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
  - Also refreshes the `AbhaLink.profile` snapshot when this ABHA is linked.

**Patient ABHA link** (nested on the patient router; reuse the patient permissions)

- `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/` → `{linked:false}` or `{linked:true, id, abha_number, abha_address, abha_addresses, kyc_verified, profile, source, verification_method, linked_by:{id,username,first_name,last_name}, linked_at}`
  - Requires read permission on the patient.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/link/` → the linked object above
  - Body: `{transaction_id}` **or**, in Phase B, `{profile_share: uuid}`.
  - Requires write permission on the patient.
  - Idempotent for the same ABHA, which refreshes the snapshot.
  - Returns 400 `abha_linked_to_other_patient` or `patient_already_linked` on conflict.
  - Sets `AbhaConsent.patient` for the transaction's consent.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/unlink/` → `{linked:false}`
  - Requires write permission.
  - Soft-deletes the link and removes the mirrored identifiers.

**Facility ABDM config** (Phase B)

- `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → `{configured:false}` or `{configured:true, hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}], share_urls:[{counter, url}]}`
- `PUT /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → same shape
  - Body: `{hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}]}`.
  - Requires the existing facility-update permission.

**Profile shares** (Phase B)

- `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/shares/?status=&date=` → paginated `[{id, token_number, counter_code, abha_number, abha_address, profile, status, patient:{id,name}|null, created_date, expires_at}]`
  - Default: today, newest first.
- `POST /api/v3/hip/patient/share` (**public**; gateway-JWT verified)
  - Mounted at the URL root in `config/urls.py`, so the bridge URL registered with ABDM is the backend's base URL.
  - Idempotent on `REQUEST-ID`.
  - On receipt:
    - If the ABHA is already linked to a patient, set status `linked` with that patient.
    - Otherwise set status `pending`.
  - Then send on-share from a Celery task.

---

## 7. Frontend journey (care_fe core; no plugin)

Gate everything on `GET /api/v1/abdm/config/` returning `enabled`. When ABDM is disabled, CARE looks unchanged.

### Placements

1. **Patient registration (create mode).**
   - Before the form, show an **ABHA step**: "Verify or create ABHA", plus "Continue without ABHA".
   - On success, prefill the form from `AbhaProfile`:
     - Name, DOB/year of birth and gender are **locked** when `kyc_verified`.
     - Phone, address, pincode and state/district are editable. Match the state and district to CARE
       govt organisations by name on a best-effort basis; the user confirms.
   - Show a small "from ABHA" provenance marker on each prefilled field.
   - Submit creates the patient as today, then calls `POST /patient/{id}/abha/link/`.
     If the link fails, the patient remains and a toast offers to retry the link from the patient page.
   - If `existing_patient` is set after verification, show "This ABHA is already linked to <name>".
     Offer "Open patient" when `can_view` is true. Do not let the user register a duplicate.
2. **Patient details page.** Replace the commented-out ABHA block in
   `src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx` with an ABHA section.
   - **Linked:** show the number, address, KYC badge, source, and who linked it and when.
     - Actions: "Show ABHA card", "Update mobile", "Unlink" (with confirmation).
     - "Show ABHA card" and "Update mobile" first run the identify flow, prefilled with the linked
       ABHA number, to get a fresh verified transaction. The browser never holds an ABDM token.
   - **Not linked:** "Link ABHA" opens the identify flow, then links.
     If the profile's demographics differ from the patient's, show the differences before confirming.
3. **Facility settings (Phase B).** An ABDM section to edit the HIP ID, HIP name and counters,
   and to display or print each counter's share QR (`qrcode.react`).
4. **Facility "ABHA shares" queue (Phase B).** Today's shares with token, name, ABHA and status.
   - "Register" opens registration prefilled from the share; after create, link with `{profile_share}`.
   - "Open patient" when the share is already linked.

### Identify flow

A single reusable component, e.g. a Sheet or Dialog with steps, used by placements 1 and 2.

1. **Identifier step.**
   - The user picks the identifier type: ABHA number, ABHA address, mobile or Aadhaar.
   - Show a "Forgot ABHA? Find by mobile" link.
   - Show "Not now" or "Continue without ABHA" everywhere it makes sense.
   - Aadhaar input:
     - Show the **full consent text verbatim** (from `config.consent.text`) above a required "I agree" checkbox.
     - The submit button stays disabled until the box is ticked.
     - Never echo the full Aadhaar back. Mask it, showing only the last 4 digits.
2. **Auth method step** (ABHA number or address only): Aadhaar OTP or mobile OTP.
   Keep the choice of identifier separate from the choice of auth method.
3. **OTP step.**
   - Show `message` and `masked_mobile` ("OTP sent to ******1234").
   - Six-digit OTP input.
   - Resend countdown of 60 s and at most 2 resends, both driven by `resend` from the server.
4. **Account chooser** when `status = "select_account"`.
5. **Not found (`abha_not_found`).**
   - Title the screen for both outcomes.
   - If the identifier was Aadhaar, offer "Create ABHA with this Aadhaar". Reuse the Aadhaar and the
     consent already given ("never ask twice"), then call `create/otp`.
   - For other identifiers, offer creation via Aadhaar. Ask only for Aadhaar plus consent, then
     **still look it up first** with `otp/request` `identifier_type=aadhaar`; create only on another `abha_not_found`.
   - **Aadhaar always starts on the login path**: `otp/request` with `identifier_type=aadhaar`.
     - The catalogue atom `hiecm.concept.m1-avoiding-duplicate-abha` says a login for an identifier nobody holds
       returns 404 `ABDM-1114` with **no OTP sent**. So lookup first costs exactly one OTP in both outcomes.
     - Wiring Aadhaar straight to enrolment is the documented cause of duplicate ABHAs.
     - A short-lived revision on 2026-10-14 said otherwise. It was reverted the same day.
   - `create/verify` must still handle `is_new:false` as a safety net:
     - `mobile_verification_required:false`
     - `abha_address_required` only if the profile has no address
     - a linkable, verified transaction
6. **Create steps.**
   1. OTP plus mobile number.
   2. Mobile OTP, if `mobile_verification_required`.
   3. Address: pick a suggestion or type one (suffix `@{cm_id}`); skippable if one already exists.
7. **Result.**
   - Profile card: photo, name, gender, DOB, ABHA number, address, mobile, KYC badge.
   - Actions: "Download ABHA card", "Show QR", and the primary action of the placement
     ("Use for registration" or "Link to patient").

### Behaviour rules

- **Never ask twice.** Keep a per-flow fact store in component state so values entered once
  (Aadhaar, mobile, ABHA number) are reused across steps and fallback paths.
- **Errors appear inline on the step in view.** Use the typed `errors[0].type`, with `silent`
  requests or a local `onError`, instead of global toasts. Never phrase a refusal as the
  patient's fault. Only `abha_not_found` ever offers creation.
- Use react-query mutations and queries with API definitions in the style of
  `src/types/emr/patient/patientApi.ts` (new files, e.g. `src/types/abdm/abdm.ts` and
  `src/types/abdm/abdmApi.ts`).
- Put every string in `public/locale/en.json` (i18n). Follow AGENTS.md and the existing shadcn/ui components.

---

## 8. Consent text (exact; the backend serves it from `GET /abdm/config/`)

Code `abha-enrollment`, version `1.4`, title "Terms and Conditions":

> I, hereby declare that I am voluntarily sharing my Aadhaar number and demographic information issued by UIDAI, with National Health Authority (NHA) for the sole purpose of creation of ABHA number. I understand that my ABHA number can be used and shared for purposes as may be notified by ABDM from time to time including provision of healthcare services. Further, I am aware that my personal identifiable information (Name, Address, Age, Date of Birth, Gender and Photograph) may be made available to the entities working in the National Digital Health Ecosystem (NDHE) which inter alia includes stakeholders and entities such as healthcare professionals (e.g. doctors), facilities (e.g. hospitals, laboratories) and data fiduciaries (e.g. health programmes), which are registered with or linked to the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), and various processes there under. I authorize NHA to use my Aadhaar number for performing Aadhaar based authentication with UIDAI as per the provisions of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 for the aforesaid purpose. I understand that UIDAI will share my e-KYC details, or response of “Yes” with NHA upon successful authentication. I have been duly informed about the option of using other IDs apart from Aadhaar; however, I consciously choose to use Aadhaar number for the purpose of availing benefits across the NDHE. I am aware that my personal identifiable information excluding Aadhaar number / VID number can be used and shared for purposes as mentioned above. I reserve the right to revoke the given consent at any point of time as per provisions of Aadhaar Act and Regulations.

Take the text from the `hiecm.concept.m1-abha-consent` atom (`abdm-docs-get`), and keep the curly quotes around “Yes”.

## 9. Local environment & verification plan

The user's own servers are running. **Do not touch them**:

- care runserver on :8000
- care_fe vite on :4000
- experience on :8001
- databases `care`, `care_abdm_*` and `test_care*`

  Base the branch on `origin/develop`, at `3fe704930` or newer.

# ABDM M1 in CARE core — shared design & API contract (v1)

Owner: coordinator chat `266e5a78-c2c5-42f4-a64a-63b291f5d5fa`.
Consumers: the backend session (repo `care`) and the frontend session (repo `care_fe`).
If an implementation must deviate from this contract, the backend reports the final
shape to the coordinator, and the coordinator relays it to the frontend.

**Ground rules**

- Build ABDM M1 into **CARE core**. Do not build it as a plugin.
- Ignore every previous attempt:
  - the `jacobjeevan-abdm-m1-core-*` branches
  - the `care_abdm` and `care_abdm_fe` plugins
  - any earlier design docs
- Do not read or copy from those attempts. Start fresh from upstream `develop`.
- Real ABDM **sandbox** credentials exist. Never commit them.
- Never put `ABDM_CLIENT_SECRET` anywhere in the frontend.

The ABDM docs MCP (`abdm-docs-*` tools, https://docs.abdm.gov.in/mcp) is available in every
session. It is the source of truth for ABDM request and response shapes:

- `abdm-docs-search` (`kind: operation`, `module: m1`) finds an operation.
- `abdm-docs-get <operationId>` returns its exact contract.
- `abdm-docs-validate` (`kind: request`) checks a request body before you send it.
- `abdm-docs-decode_error` explains any error you get back from ABDM.

---

## 1. Scope

### Must (Phase A)

1. **One identify screen with two outcomes.** A desk user never chooses between "log in" and
   "create". They pick an identifier, and the ABDM response decides what happens next.
2. **Verify an existing ABHA.** Every method below is mandatory in M1 testing:
   - Mobile number + mobile OTP. ABDM may return several accounts, so show an account chooser.
   - Aadhaar number + Aadhaar OTP.
   - ABHA number + Aadhaar OTP, or ABHA number + mobile OTP.
   - ABHA address + Aadhaar OTP, or ABHA address + mobile OTP. This uses the PHR web-login API family.
3. **Find a forgotten ABHA by mobile.** ABDM returns a masked list without sending an OTP. The user
   picks one entry, chooses an OTP method, and verifies.
4. **Create an ABHA from Aadhaar only.** This step runs only after a lookup has returned `ABDM-1114`.
   - Show the consent text verbatim, with an "I agree" checkbox.
   - Request the Aadhaar OTP.
   - Enrol with the OTP and the mobile number.
   - If the mobile differs from the Aadhaar-linked one, verify it with a mobile OTP.
   - Show ABHA address suggestions and let the user create an address.
5. **Show the profile, the ABHA card and the QR code** for a verified session.
6. **Link a verified ABHA to a CARE patient.**
   - Prefill registration from the profile. Lock name, DOB and gender when the profile is KYC verified.
   - When registering, create the patient first, then link.
   - Link an ABHA to an existing patient from the patient page.
   - Unlink.
   - Mirror the ABHA number and address as patient identifiers so the existing patient search finds them.
7. **Update the mobile number** on the ABHA account from the patient page. Verify first, then change it.
8. **Consent audit records.** Record who agreed, when, which version, and for which transaction or patient.
9. **Resend OTP.** Allow at most 2 resends, each no sooner than 60 s after the last send.
   Enforce this on the server and show it in the UI.

### Should (Phase B: same branch, after Phase A is complete and tested)

10. **Facility ABDM configuration.**
    - Store the HIP ID (the HFR facility id registered on the bridge), a HIP name and counter codes.
    - Show a counter QR that points to `{ABDM_PHR_SHARE_URL}?hip-id=<HIP_ID>&counter-id=<COUNTER>`.
11. **Scan & share (profile share).**
    - ABDM calls `POST /api/v3/hip/patient/share` on our bridge. Reply 200 at once.
    - Then call `{GATEWAY}/api/hiecm/patient-share/v3/on-share` asynchronously, within 30 s.
      The acknowledgement carries the token number.
    - Build a facility queue of shares. From the queue, the user can register and link a patient,
      or open the already-linked patient.

### Not now (record as deliberately deferred; do not build)

- Biometric, face and demographic authentication.
- Child ABHA.
- Scanning an ABHA card QR with the camera.
- Email update.
- Password login.
- ABHA deactivation or deletion.
- Benefit linking.
- Mobile- or DL-based creation. This is forbidden: creation is **only** from Aadhaar.
  Guard it in code with an explicit refusal.
- Everything in M2 and M3: care contexts, HIP-initiated linking, consent and data flow.

---

{"body":"# What an ABHA address is allowed to be

## In plain words

ABHA Addresses must comply with defined validation standards.

**Permitted Characters**

- Alphabetic characters (A-Z)
- Numeric characters (0-9)
- Dot (.)

**Validation Rules**

- Cannot begin with a numeric character.
- Cannot begin or end with a dot (.).
- Must conform to ABDM validation requirements at the time of creation.
- Mobile numbers cannot be used directly as ABHA Addresses.

Organizations should rely on ABDM validation services to verify address eligibility.

Every ABHA number is issued a default address built from its 14 digits. A person cannot create that address themselves, and can create a readable one beside it. Offer addresses built from the person's name rather than an empty field.

## Before you start

Know whether the address is being created against an ABHA number or against a mobile number with a self declared profile. See [P1 Registration and login](/docs/hiecm/v3/milestones/p1).

## What happens

Validate the rules above in your own form before you submit, so a refused address becomes an inline message. Offer the suggestions the service returns from `/abha/api/v3/enrollment/enrol/suggestion` during M1 enrolment. Send the chosen address without the `@` suffix where the call asks for it.

## How you know it worked

The address is created and the person can sign in with it. Before that, your form refuses an address that begins with a digit, begins or ends with a dot, or is a mobile number.

## When it goes wrong

The address is taken: show alternatives rather than an error alone. The person expects to use their mobile number as their address: say in the form that this is not allowed, rather than letting them find out on submission.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"/docs/hiecm/v3/registries/abha#abha-address-policy","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.abha-address-policy","milestone":"M1","summary":"The characters and shapes an ABHA address may take, and the default address every ABHA number is issued.","title":"What an ABHA address is allowed to be","type":"concept"}

content.text:
From the coordinator: UX rules from the ABDM catalogue atoms `m1-never-ask-twice`, `m1-screen-contract` and `m1-honest-screen-states`. Design doc §7 "Behaviour rules" is updated. They refine "never ask twice"; please build them in. No reply needed.

1. **Write-once facts with provenance.**
   - The fact store holds `{value, provenance}` per fact.
   - Every prefilled field in the flow, not only the registration form, shows where it came from: "from the mobile you entered earlier", "from patient record", "from ABHA".
   - Nothing silently overwrites a fact.
2. **A failed route gives back what it collected.** Example: a patient identifies by mobile, gets `abha_not_found`, then "Create ABHA" asks only for Aadhaar plus consent and runs the lookup first. The create OTP step's "Mobile number for ABHA communication" is then **prefilled** from that mobile, with provenance shown.
3. **Patient-page placement.** Prefill the mobile identifier from `patient.phone_number`, with provenance "from patient record", so the desk doesn't retype it.
4. **No state survives into the next patient.** Reset the whole fact store and all hand-typed inputs whenever the flow is closed or restarted. The leak is usually a hand-typed field.
5. **Inactive steps are inert.** Render only the active step, or set `inert` on the hidden ones, so the tab order never walks into invisible fields.
6. **`abha_not_found` can also come from `otp/verify`.** ABDM may only discover "no account" for a mobile after the OTP. Send it to the same not-found screen.
7. **Resend.** Always call `otp/resend {transaction_id}` with the current transaction; never a fresh `otp/request`. Show a visible countdown, and disable the button while waiting.
8. **Account chooser.** Required, not an edge case; family phones carry several ABHAs. Show what each account carries (name, ABHA number, address) and ask nothing else.

## 6. REST API contract (backend implements; frontend consumes)

All endpoints are under `/api/v1/` and use CARE JWT auth unless marked otherwise.

### 6.1 Error shape

All errors use CARE's existing envelope, so `handleHttpError` keeps working:

```json
{"errors": [{"type": "abha_not_found", "msg": "No ABHA was found for this identifier.", "abdm_code": "ABDM-1114", "loc": ["value"], "retry_after_seconds": null}]}
```

| HTTP | `type` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `validation_error` | Our input validation failed (pydantic; `loc` set). |
| 400 | `abdm_validation_error` | ABDM refused a field. `loc` holds our field name; `msg` is ABDM's message, worded so it never blames the patient. |
| 400 | `invalid_otp` / `otp_expired` | |
| 400 | `transaction_expired` / `invalid_state` | Wrong step for this transaction, or the transaction expired. |
| 400 | `consent_required` | Aadhaar was sent without `consent.agreed=true` and the current version. |
| 400 | `abha_linked_to_other_patient` | Include `patient: {id, name, can_view}`. |
| 400 | `patient_already_linked` | The patient is already linked to a **different** ABHA. |
| 400 | `creation_method_not_allowed` | Anything other than Aadhaar was used to create. |
| 404 | `abha_not_found` | **Only** for `ABDM-1114`. |
| 404 | `transaction_not_found` | |
| 429 | `resend_too_soon` | Includes `retry_after_seconds`. |
| 429 | `resend_limit_reached` | |
| 502 | `abdm_unavailable` | Network error, timeout, or ABDM 5xx. |
| 502 | `abdm_error` | Unclassified ABDM refusal; `abdm_code` and `msg` pass through. |
| 502 | `abdm_session_expired` | The X-token expired. The frontend restarts verification. |
| 503 | `abdm_disabled` | |

Never return HTTP 401 or 403 for an ABDM-side auth failure. The frontend treats 401 as "CARE session expired".

### 6.2 Shared shapes

```ts
type AbhaProfile = {
  abha_number: string | null;          // "91-1234-5678-9012"
  abha_address: string | null;         // preferred, e.g. "john.doe@sbx"
  abha_addresses: string[];
  name: string; first_name: string | null; middle_name: string | null; last_name: string | null;
  gender: "male" | "female" | "transgender" | "non_binary" | null; // CARE vocabulary
  abdm_gender: string | null;          // raw "M" | "F" | "O" | "T" | "D" | "U"
  date_of_birth: string | null;        // "YYYY-MM-DD" when the full DOB is known
  year_of_birth: number | null;
  mobile: string | null;               // 10 digits
  email: string | null;
  address: string | null; pincode: string | null;
  state_name: string | null; state_code: string | null;
  district_name: string | null; district_code: string | null;
  kyc_verified: boolean;
  status: string | null;               // "ACTIVE" etc.
  photo: string | null;                // base64 JPEG; returned live, NEVER stored
};
type AbhaAccount = {                  // account chooser row (verify may return several)
  abha_number: string | null; abha_address: string | null; name: string;
  gender: string | null; kyc_verified: boolean | null; status: string | null; photo: string | null;
};
type OtpSent = {
  transaction_id: string;              // our opaque uuid
  message: string;                     // ABDM's message, safe to show
  masked_mobile: string | null;        // e.g. "******1234", parsed from the message
  otp_system: "aadhaar" | "abdm";
  resend: { available_in_seconds: number; remaining: number }; // 60 and 2 after the first send
};
type ExistingPatient = { id: string; name: string; can_view: boolean } | null;
type Verified = {
  transaction_id: string;
  status: "verified" | "select_account";
  accounts: AbhaAccount[];             // filled when status = "select_account"
  profile: AbhaProfile | null;         // filled when status = "verified"
  existing_patient: ExistingPatient;   // a CARE patient already linked to this ABHA
};
```

### 6.3 Endpoints

**Configuration**

- `GET /api/v1/abdm/config/`
  - Returns `{enabled, cm_id, abha_address_suffix, consent:{code, version, text}, otp:{length:6, resend_wait_seconds:60, max_resends:2}}`.
  - `consent.text` is the exact ABDM consent text from §8. The backend owns it.

**Identify (login, verify)**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/request/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{identifier_type:"mobile"|"aadhaar"|"abha_number"|"abha_address", value, otp_system?:"aadhaar"|"abdm", consent?:{agreed:true, version:"1.4"}, facility?:uuid}`.
  - `otp_system` is required for `abha_number` and `abha_address`. For the other identifiers it is implied: `aadhaar` → `aadhaar`, `mobile` → `abdm`.
  - `consent` is **required** when `identifier_type="aadhaar"`. The Aadhaar consent is shown before any Aadhaar leaves the browser, and an `AbhaConsent` row is recorded with purpose `aadhaar_verification`.
  - Values: Aadhaar is 12 digits (Verhoeff check). Mobile is 10 digits starting 6–9. The ABHA number is 14 digits, with or without hyphens. The ABHA address may omit the `@sbx` suffix; the backend appends `@{cm_id}`.
  - Returns 404 `abha_not_found` when ABDM answers `ABDM-1114`. In that case no OTP was sent, and the frontend offers creation.
  - For `identifier_type="mobile"`, the backend first calls the **free** search `POST /v3/profile/account/abha/search`. That call sends no OTP.
    - On `ABDM-1114` it returns `abha_not_found` before any OTP is spent.
    - Otherwise it sends the mobile login OTP as before. The search's `txnId` is discarded.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/resend/`
  - Body: `{transaction_id}`. Works for any OTP step: login, find, create, create-mobile and update-mobile.
  - Returns `OtpSent`, or 429.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/otp/verify/` → `Verified`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`. For login and find flows.
  - May also return 404 `abha_not_found`. The login-verify docs say `ABDM-1114` at verify means "no account matched", for example
    a mobile holding no ABHA. The frontend then shows the same not-found screen; the mobile is already in the fact store.
  - The backend also returns `abha_not_found` when verify succeeds with an empty `accounts` list.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/select-account/` → `Verified` (status `verified`)
  - Body: `{transaction_id, abha_number}`.

**Find**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/find/`
  - Body: `{mobile}`.
  - Returns `{transaction_id, accounts:[{index, abha_number (masked), name (masked), gender, kyc_verified, auth_methods:["AADHAAR_OTP","MOBILE_OTP",...]}]}`.
  - Returns 404 `abha_not_found` when ABDM finds none.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/find/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, index, otp_system:"aadhaar"|"abdm"}`.
  - Then call `otp/verify`.

**Create (Aadhaar only)**

- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{aadhaar, consent:{agreed:true, version:"1.4"}, facility?}`.
  - Records `AbhaConsent` with purpose `abha_creation`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/verify/`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp, mobile}`.
  - Returns `{transaction_id, is_new, profile: AbhaProfile, mobile_verification_required: boolean, abha_address_required: boolean, existing_patient}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/verify/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address-suggestions/?transaction_id=`
  - Returns `{suggestions: string[]}`, without the suffix.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, abha_address}`, without the suffix.

**Verified-session operations** (any flow that reached `enrolled` or `verified`)

- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/?transaction_id=` → `{profile}` (refetched live)
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/card/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
  - `data` is base64 of the official ABHA card. For the address path, this is the PHR card.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/qr/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/verify/` → `{profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
  - Also refreshes the `AbhaLink.profile` snapshot when this ABHA is linked.

**Patient ABHA link** (nested on the patient router; reuse the patient permissions)

- `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/` → `{linked:false}` or `{linked:true, id, abha_number, abha_address, abha_addresses, kyc_verified, profile, source, verification_method, linked_by:{id,username,first_name,last_name}, linked_at}`
  - Requires read permission on the patient.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/link/` → the linked object above
  - Body: `{transaction_id}` **or**, in Phase B, `{profile_share: uuid}`.
  - Requires write permission on the patient.
  - Idempotent for the same ABHA, which refreshes the snapshot.
  - Returns 400 `abha_linked_to_other_patient` or `patient_already_linked` on conflict.
  - Sets `AbhaConsent.patient` for the transaction's consent.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/unlink/` → `{linked:false}`
  - Requires write permission.
  - Soft-deletes the link and removes the mirrored identifiers.

**Facility ABDM config** (Phase B)

- `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → `{configured:false}` or `{configured:true, hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}], share_urls:[{counter, url}]}`
- `PUT /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → same shape
  - Body: `{hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}]}`.
  - Requires the existing facility-update permission.

   - Show a small "from ABHA" provenance marker on each prefilled field.
   - Submit creates the patient as today, then calls `POST /patient/{id}/abha/link/`.
     If the link fails, the patient remains and a toast offers to retry the link from the patient page.
   - If `existing_patient` is set after verification, show "This ABHA is already linked to <name>".
     Offer "Open patient" when `can_view` is true. Do not let the user register a duplicate.
2. **Patient details page.** Replace the commented-out ABHA block in
   `src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx` with an ABHA section.
   - **Linked:** show the number, address, KYC badge, source, and who linked it and when.
     - Actions: "Show ABHA card", "Update mobile", "Unlink" (with confirmation).
     - "Show ABHA card" and "Update mobile" first run the identify flow, prefilled with the linked
       ABHA number, to get a fresh verified transaction. The browser never holds an ABDM token.
   - **Not linked:** "Link ABHA" opens the identify flow, then links.
     If the profile's demographics differ from the patient's, show the differences before confirming.
3. **Facility settings (Phase B).** An ABDM section to edit the HIP ID, HIP name and counters,
   and to display or print each counter's share QR (`qrcode.react`).
4. **Facility "ABHA shares" queue (Phase B).** Today's shares with token, name, ABHA and status.
   - "Register" opens registration prefilled from the share; after create, link with `{profile_share}`.
   - "Open patient" when the share is already linked.

### Identify flow

A single reusable component, e.g. a Sheet or Dialog with steps, used by placements 1 and 2.

1. **Identifier step.**
   - The user picks the identifier type: ABHA number, ABHA address, mobile or Aadhaar.
   - Show a "Forgot ABHA? Find by mobile" link.
   - Show "Not now" or "Continue without ABHA" everywhere it makes sense.
   - Aadhaar input:
     - Show the **full consent text verbatim** (from `config.consent.text`) above a required "I agree" checkbox.
     - The submit button stays disabled until the box is ticked.
     - Never echo the full Aadhaar back. Mask it, showing only the last 4 digits.
2. **Auth method step** (ABHA number or address only): Aadhaar OTP or mobile OTP.
   Keep the choice of identifier separate from the choice of auth method.
3. **OTP step.**
   - Show `message` and `masked_mobile` ("OTP sent to ******1234").
   - Six-digit OTP input.
   - Resend countdown of 60 s and at most 2 resends, both driven by `resend` from the server.
4. **Account chooser** when `status = "select_account"`.
5. **Not found (`abha_not_found`).**
   - Title the screen for both outcomes.
   - If the identifier was Aadhaar, offer "Create ABHA with this Aadhaar". Reuse the Aadhaar and the
     consent already given ("never ask twice"), then call `create/otp`.
   - For other identifiers, offer creation via Aadhaar. Ask only for Aadhaar plus consent, then
     **still look it up first** with `otp/request` `identifier_type=aadhaar`; create only on another `abha_not_found`.
   - **Aadhaar always starts on the login path**: `otp/request` with `identifier_type=aadhaar`.
     - The catalogue atom `hiecm.concept.m1-avoiding-duplicate-abha` says a login for an identifier nobody holds
       returns 404 `ABDM-1114` with **no OTP sent**. So lookup first costs exactly one OTP in both outcomes.
     - Wiring Aadhaar straight to enrolment is the documented cause of duplicate ABHAs.
     - A short-lived revision on 2026-10-14 said otherwise. It was reverted the same day.
   - `create/verify` must still handle `is_new:false` as a safety net:
     - `mobile_verification_required:false`
     - `abha_address_required` only if the profile has no address
     - a linkable, verified transaction
6. **Create steps.**
   1. OTP plus mobile number.
   2. Mobile OTP, if `mobile_verification_required`.
   3. Address: pick a suggestion or type one (suffix `@{cm_id}`); skippable if one already exists.
7. **Result.**
   - Profile card: photo, name, gender, DOB, ABHA number, address, mobile, KYC badge.
   - Actions: "Download ABHA card", "Show QR", and the primary action of the placement
     ("Use for registration" or "Link to patient").

### Behaviour rules

- **Never ask twice.** Keep a per-flow fact store in component state so values entered once
  (Aadhaar, mobile, ABHA number) are reused across steps and fallback paths.
  These rules come from the catalogue atoms `m1-never-ask-twice`, `m1-screen-contract` and `m1-honest-screen-states`.
  - **Facts are write-once,** and each carries its **provenance**, for example "from the mobile you entered" or
    "from the patient record". Show provenance beside every prefilled field, in the flow as well as on the form.
  - **A failed route gives back what it collected.** Mobile → not found → create: the create OTP step's
    "mobile for ABHA communication" is prefilled from that mobile, and the identify-step Aadhaar carries into creation.
  - **Patient-page placement.** Prefill the mobile identifier from `patient.phone_number`, with provenance "from patient record".
  - **No state survives into the next patient.** Reset the whole fact store and every hand-typed field whenever the flow is closed or restarted.
  - **Inactive steps are inert.** Render only the active step, or mark the others `inert`, so nothing hidden sits in the tab order.
  - The account chooser asks nothing the accounts already carry.
  - Resend calls `otp/resend` with the same `transaction_id`; never start a new `otp/request`. Show a visible countdown.
- **Errors appear inline on the step in view.** Use the typed `errors[0].type`, with `silent`
  requests or a local `onError`, instead of global toasts. Never phrase a refusal as the
  patient's fault. Only `abha_not_found` ever offers creation.
  - `abha_not_found` may arrive at `otp/verify` as well as at `otp/request`. Route both to the same not-found screen.
- Use react-query mutations and queries with API definitions in the style of
  `src/types/emr/patient/patientApi.ts` (new files, e.g. `src/types/abdm/abdm.ts` and
  `src/types/abdm/abdmApi.ts`).
- Put every string in `public/locale/en.json` (i18n). Follow AGENTS.md and the existing shadcn/ui components.

---

{"body":"# The ABHA step comes before the registration form and fills it

## In plain words

An ABHA is a patient's health account, and a verified one already holds their
name, date of birth, gender, mobile number, full address with its codes, and a
photograph. A desk that reads that profile types almost nothing.

Put the ABHA step first and the registration form opens already filled. Put it
second and you have spent the keystrokes the integration existed to save, then
filed an identifier on top of them.

The test is simple. Count what the receptionist typed. If a registration with an
ABHA took as many keystrokes as one without, the order of the screens is the
first thing to look at.

## Before you start

- A client that can call the M1 operations, holding a session token.
- A decision about which routes your deployment offers, which
  [the deployment interview](m1-deployment-interview.md) settles.
- Somewhere to put the facts a route returns, which
  [the patient fact store](m1-never-ask-twice.md) describes.

## What happens

Rank what is scarce at a counter. Calls are cheap. In order of cost:

1. **Questions put to the patient.** A third question costs more than three
   extra HTTP calls.
2. **One time passwords.** They fail, they expire, they lock a transaction, and
   they reach a handset the person may not be holding.
3. **API calls.** Last, and a long way last.

Rank routes by that list in order, and never let a call count outrank a
question.

| Route | Questions | One time passwords | Calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scan and register | 0 | 0 | 1 out, 1 in |
| Create, demographic authentication | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Create, fingerprint | 1 | 0 | 1 to 3 |
| Create, face | 1 | 0 | 3 plus polling |
| Log in, any identifier | 1 | 1 | 3 to 4 |
| Create, Aadhaar one time password | 1 to 2 | 1 to 2 | 4 to 5 |

Two things fall out of that table.

Demographic authentication is one call and spends no one time password. A
government integrator is required to offer it and a private integrator is not
asked for it, so most integrators build the five call route instead, because it
is the one the specification leads with.

The cheapest journey involves no desk call at all. A registered facility with a
callback ABDM can reach can put a QR code at the counter, and the profile
arrives already consented.

Some lookups cost nothing. A login attempt on an identifier nobody holds is
refused `ABDM-1114` before any one time password is sent, so looking before
creating is free for exactly the people you would otherwise send to create a
duplicate.

## How you know it worked

A receptionist registering a patient who brought an ABHA types corrections only.
Every field the profile carries arrives filled, and the only screen asking for
input is the one confirming the form.

Count the one time passwords spent on a full registration. On the demographic
route and on scan and register that count is zero.

## When it goes wrong

- The form opens empty after a successful ABHA step. The profile was read and
  its result was not carried into the form. Hold it in the fact store rather
  than in a screen's own state, which
  [the patient fact store](m1-never-ask-twice.md) covers.
- The desk asks for an identifier it already holds. Same cause, same fix.
- The journey offers login or creation as a question to the patient. They often
  cannot answer it, and
  [avoiding a duplicate ABHA](m1-avoiding-duplicate-abha.md) explains what to
  do instead.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.m1-counter-journey-order","milestone":"M1","summary":"Ask for an ABHA before you ask a patient to register, because a verified profile already carries the answers the form is asking for.","title":"The ABHA step comes before the registration form and fills it","type":"concept"}

From the coordinator: **the backend is ready on http://localhost:9100.** It's on branch `jacobjeevan-abdm-m1-abha-backend`, and my independent OTP-free checks pass 25 of 25.

**Login**
- **admin / admin:** superuser. It sees the 10 seeded patients, for example the facility "FACILITY WITH PATIENTS" `d53f2a67-894b-450d-a633-de9ba1e9c9b9`.
- care-admin / Ohcn@123 also logs in, but sees no patients.

**Live behaviour I verified, against the real sandbox, with no OTP sent**
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/config/` matches §6. The consent text is verbatim, 1692 chars.
- `find` with an unknown mobile → 404 `abha_not_found`.
- `otp/request` → 404 `abha_not_found` for:
  - an unknown `abha_address`, with or without `@sbx`
  - an unknown mobile; the free pre-search runs first, so no OTP is sent
- Aadhaar without consent, or failing the Verhoeff check → 400 `validation_error`. The same holds for `create/otp`.
- A malformed mobile or ABHA number → 400 `validation_error`.
- An unknown `transaction_id` on verify, resend, select-account, profile or patient link → 404 `transaction_not_found`.
- `GET /api/v1/patient/{id}/abha/` → `{"linked":false}`.

**Contract additions; please handle them**
1. `config.consent.title` exists ("Terms and Conditions"); the extra field is harmless.
2. **New error `rate_limited`** (429, with `retry_after_seconds` and a `Retry-After` header). The cap is 15 `otp/request` attempts per user per 10 minutes, and not-found attempts count.
   - Show a "try again in N" message. Keep it distinct from `resend_too_soon` and `resend_limit_reached`.
3. 400 `validation_error` never echoes the input back.
4. **One account: the mobile login finishes inside `otp/verify` and returns `status:"verified"`.** The backend still makes ABDM's select-account call for it. Show the chooser only when `status === "select_account"`.
5. Anonymous requests get 403, CARE's default, not 401. This doesn't change how you handle errors.

**Testing**
- For the Playwright `page.route` fixtures, capture real responses from :9100 on the free paths: config, `abha_not_found`, `validation_error` and `transaction_not_found`. The mocks then match the real envelope exactly.
- Go easy on `otp/request` in manual smoke tests because of the rate limit.
- Never request an OTP for a real Aadhaar, mobile or ABHA.

When you finish, send me a short report. Include the branch, commits, check results (typecheck, lint, build, Playwright) and the dev-server PID on :4100.

### Bridge callback

`POST /api/v3/hip/patient/share` (path relative to the registered bridge URL):

- Headers: `REQUEST-ID`, `TIMESTAMP`, `X-HIP-ID`, `Authorization` (gateway JWT).
- Body:
  - `intent: "PROFILE_SHARE"`
  - `metaData: {hipId, context}`, where `context` is the counter id
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp, mobile}`.
  - Returns `{transaction_id, is_new, profile: AbhaProfile, mobile_verification_required: boolean, abha_address_required: boolean, existing_patient}`.
  - `abha_address_required`:
    - `is_new:true` → always `true`. The ABDM default address does not count (see §7 step 6).
    - `is_new:false` → `true` only when the profile has no address at all.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/mobile/verify/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address-suggestions/?transaction_id=`
  - Returns `{suggestions: string[]}`, without the suffix.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/create/address/` → `{transaction_id, profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, abha_address}`, without the suffix.

**Verified-session operations** (any flow that reached `enrolled` or `verified`)

- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/?transaction_id=` → `{profile}` (refetched live)
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/card/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
  - `data` is base64 of the official ABHA card. For the address path, this is the PHR card.
- `GET /api/v1/abdm/abha/qr/?transaction_id=` → `{content_type, data}`
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/otp/` → `OtpSent`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, mobile}`.
- `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/profile/mobile/verify/` → `{profile}`
  - Body: `{transaction_id, otp}`.
  - Also refreshes the `AbhaLink.profile` snapshot when this ABHA is linked.

**Patient ABHA link** (nested on the patient router; reuse the patient permissions)

- `GET /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/` → `{linked:false}` or `{linked:true, id, abha_number, abha_address, abha_addresses, kyc_verified, profile, source, verification_method, linked_by:{id,username,first_name,last_name}, linked_at}`
  - Requires read permission on the patient.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/link/` → the linked object above
  - Body: `{transaction_id}` **or**, in Phase B, `{profile_share: uuid}`.
  - Requires write permission on the patient.
  - Idempotent for the same ABHA, which refreshes the snapshot.
  - Returns 400 `abha_linked_to_other_patient` or `patient_already_linked` on conflict.
  - Sets `AbhaConsent.patient` for the transaction's consent.
- `POST /api/v1/patient/{patient_id}/abha/unlink/` → `{linked:false}`
  - Requires write permission.
  - Soft-deletes the link and removes the mirrored identifiers.

**Facility ABDM config** (Phase B)

- `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → `{configured:false}` or `{configured:true, hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}], share_urls:[{counter, url}]}`
- `PUT /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/` → same shape
  - Body: `{hip_id, hip_name, counters:[{code,name}]}`.
  - Requires the existing facility-update permission.

**Profile shares** (Phase B)

- `GET /api/v1/facility/{facility_id}/abdm/shares/?status=&date=` → paginated `[{id, token_number, counter_code, abha_number, abha_address, profile, status, patient:{id,name}|null, created_date, expires_at}]`
  - Default: today, newest first.
- `POST /api/v3/hip/patient/share` (**public**; gateway-JWT verified)
  - Mounted at the URL root in `config/urls.py`, so the bridge URL registered with ABDM is the backend's base URL.
  - Idempotent on `REQUEST-ID`.
  - On receipt:
    - If the ABHA is already linked to a patient, set status `linked` with that patient.
    - Otherwise set status `pending`.
  - Then send on-share from a Celery task.

## 7. Frontend journey (care_fe core; no plugin)

Gate everything on `GET /api/v1/abdm/config/` returning `enabled`. When ABDM is disabled, CARE looks unchanged.

### Placements

1. **Patient registration (create mode).**
   - Before the form, show an **ABHA step**: "Verify or create ABHA", plus "Continue without ABHA".
   - On success, prefill the form from `AbhaProfile`:
     - Name, DOB/year of birth and gender are **locked** when `kyc_verified`.
     - Phone, address, pincode and state/district are editable. Match the state and district to CARE
       govt organisations by name on a best-effort basis; the user confirms.
   - Show a small "from ABHA" provenance marker on each prefilled field.
   - Submit creates the patient as today, then calls `POST /patient/{id}/abha/link/`.
     If the link fails, the patient remains and a toast offers to retry the link from the patient page.
   - If `existing_patient` is set after verification, show "This ABHA is already linked to <name>".
     Offer "Open patient" when `can_view` is true. Do not let the user register a duplicate.
2. **Patient details page.** Replace the commented-out ABHA block in
   `src/components/Patient/PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx` with an ABHA section.
   - **Linked:** show the number, address, KYC badge, source, and who linked it and when.
     - Actions: "Show ABHA card", "Update mobile", "Unlink" (with confirmation).
     - "Show ABHA card" and "Update mobile" first run the identify flow, prefilled with the linked
       ABHA number, to get a fresh verified transaction. The browser never holds an ABDM token.
   - **Not linked:** "Link ABHA" opens the identify flow, then links.
     If the profile's demographics differ from the patient's, show the differences before confirming.
3. **Facility settings (Phase B).** An ABDM section to edit the HIP ID, HIP name and counters,
   and to display or print each counter's share QR (`qrcode.react`).
4. **Facility "ABHA shares" queue (Phase B).** Today's shares with token, name, ABHA and status.
   - "Register" opens registration prefilled from the share; after create, link with `{profile_share}`.
   - "Open patient" when the share is already linked.

### Identify flow

A single reusable component, e.g. a Sheet or Dialog with steps, used by placements 1 and 2.

1. **Identifier step.**
   - The user picks the identifier type: ABHA number, ABHA address, mobile or Aadhaar.
   - Show a "Forgot ABHA? Find by mobile" link.
   - Show "Not now" or "Continue without ABHA" everywhere it makes sense.
   - Aadhaar input:
     - Show the **full consent text verbatim** (from `config.consent.text`) above a required "I agree" checkbox.
     - The submit button stays disabled until the box is ticked.
     - Never echo the full Aadhaar back. Mask it, showing only the last 4 digits.
2. **Auth method step** (ABHA number or address only): Aadhaar OTP or mobile OTP.
   Keep the choice of identifier separate from the choice of auth method.
3. **OTP step.**
   - Show `message` and `masked_mobile` ("OTP sent to ******1234").
   - Six-digit OTP input.
   - Resend countdown of 60 s and at most 2 resends, both driven by `resend` from the server.
4. **Account chooser** when `status = "select_account"`.
5. **Not found (`abha_not_found`).**
   - Title the screen for both outcomes.
   - If the identifier was Aadhaar, offer "Create ABHA with this Aadhaar". Reuse the Aadhaar and the
     consent already given ("never ask twice"), then call `create/otp`.
   - For other identifiers, offer creation via Aadhaar. Ask only for Aadhaar plus consent, then
     **still look it up first** with `otp/request` `identifier_type=aadhaar`; create only on another `abha_not_found`.
   - **Aadhaar always starts on the login path**: `otp/request` with `identifier_type=aadhaar`.
     - The catalogue atom `hiecm.concept.m1-avoiding-duplicate-abha` says a login for an identifier nobody holds
       returns 404 `ABDM-1114` with **no OTP sent**. So lookup first costs exactly one OTP in both outcomes.
     - Wiring Aadhaar straight to enrolment is the documented cause of duplicate ABHAs.
     - A short-lived revision on 2026-10-14 said otherwise. It was reverted the same day.
   - `create/verify` must still handle `is_new:false` as a safety net:
     - `mobile_verification_required:false`
     - `abha_address_required` only if the profile has no address
     - a linkable, verified transaction
6. **Create steps.**
   1. OTP plus mobile number.
   2. Mobile OTP, if `mobile_verification_required`.
   3. Address: pick a suggestion or type one (suffix `@{cm_id}`).
      - **Mandatory when `abha_address_required` is true**, with no skip.
      - **For a new ABHA (`is_new:true`) the backend always sets `abha_address_required: true`.** ABDM gives every new
        account a system default address in `ABHAProfile.phrAddress`, so "has an address" is no signal.
      - Catalogue atom `hiecm.flow.m1-create-abha-aadhaar-otp`: "An account left with only its default address is a half finished job the person will not recognise later."
      - Done means `create/address` returned the chosen address as the preferred one.

{"body":"# What an ABHA address is allowed to be

## In plain words

ABHA Addresses must comply with defined validation standards.

**Permitted Characters**

- Alphabetic characters (A-Z)
- Numeric characters (0-9)
- Dot (.)

**Validation Rules**

- Cannot begin with a numeric character.
- Cannot begin or end with a dot (.).
- Must conform to ABDM validation requirements at the time of creation.
- Mobile numbers cannot be used directly as ABHA Addresses.

Organizations should rely on ABDM validation services to verify address eligibility.

Every ABHA number is issued a default address built from its 14 digits. A person cannot create that address themselves, and can create a readable one beside it. Offer addresses built from the person's name rather than an empty field.

## Before you start

Know whether the address is being created against an ABHA number or against a mobile number with a self declared profile. See [P1 Registration and login](/docs/hiecm/v3/milestones/p1).

## What happens

Validate the rules above in your own form before you submit, so a refused address becomes an inline message. Offer the suggestions the service returns from `/abha/api/v3/enrollment/enrol/suggestion` during M1 enrolment. Send the chosen address without the `@` suffix where the call asks for it.

## How you know it worked

The address is created and the person can sign in with it. Before that, your form refuses an address that begins with a digit, begins or ends with a dot, or is a mobile number.

## When it goes wrong

The address is taken: show alternatives rather than an error alone. The person expects to use their mobile number as their address: say in the form that this is not allowed, rather than letting them find out on submission.","catalogue_version":"2026.09.16","doc_url":"/docs/hiecm/v3/registries/abha#abha-address-policy","gateway":"hiecm","id":"hiecm.concept.abha-address-policy","milestone":"M1","summary":"The characters and shapes an ABHA address may take, and the default address every ABHA number is issued.","title":"What an ABHA address is allowed to be","type":"concept"}
